text:
nate: heads-up — saw a small but persistent GPU mem growth across canary for the latest tensor-pool change. not full OOM, but long-lived allocations tying up logits slabs and scratchpads. repro on se-staging.

maria: can you paste the profile snapshot? where's it sticking (activations vs logits vs kv)?

nate: attaching quick dump:
```
PID 4321: total_gpu 24.0G used 18.9G
- logits_slab: 5.1G (expected ~3.2G)
- activation_pool: 9.8G
- scratchpad_temp: 2.6G (should be ephemeral)
- kv_cache_region: 1.4G (stable)
```
looks like logits_slab isn't releasing after short requests. measured lifetime shows many allocations with lifetime > 120s.

cheng: interesting. did we change slab retirement or freelist thresholds in the pool allocator patch? that would explain longer reuse cycles.

lina: i saw the same on a different model: small batch sizes + repeated short requests cause the pool to keep pins on logits to avoid re-zeroing, and our retire window is 5 minutes. can we reduce to 30s for small buffers?

maria: reducing retire window risks churn and extra zeroing costs. maybe add a scoped retirement for buffers < X bytes (hot path) so long-lived pins don't block small buffers.

nate: proposal: add a "scoped buffer retirement" path — buffers allocated for request-scoped tensors get a short TTL and are reclaimed eagerly by a background recycler unless re-pinned by another active request. also instrument tag with request_id and stack hint for leak detection.

cheng: implementation note: add a per-buffer bitflag (SCOPED) and a 64-bit tag (request_id). recycler scans recent allocations and if tag not active -> free. complexity: scanning overhead on big pools.

lina: cheaper approach: maintain a small LRU of scoped buffers per device that only tracks last N allocations; recycler reads that LRU and frees expired entries. avoids full-pool scans.

maria: +1 for LRU. also add a diagnostic mode (ops-bot) to emit allocation traces when we see mem growth. ops-bot: can we get that alert hook?

ops-bot: alloc-trace-hook enabled for se-staging. will post traces to #eng-runtime-alloc-traces every 15m when growth > 100MB/10m.

nate: ran a local patch with LRU recycler and 30s TTL for scoped buffers. short-run results:
```
before: steady_growth ~ 60MB/10m, peak logits_slab 5.1G
after: steady_growth ~ 3MB/10m, peak logits_slab 3.4G
latency p50/p95 unchanged (+0.4ms p50), cpu for recycler ~0.8% per-GPU thread\```
looks promising but need longer canary.

cheng: good. couple of edge cases: 1) pinned by KV prefetch/repinning, 2) re-use semantics across batched sequences where request_id changes. make sure repinning clears scoped flag so it transitions to pooled ownership.

lina: agree. also add a guard: if a buffer was scoped and repinned within TTL more than K times, promote it to permanent pool to avoid oscillation.

maria: can we add a lightweight leak detector that flags allocations with lifetime > 10x expected? cheat: track histogram of lifetimes per buffer-size-class and flag outliers.

nate: implemented a first-pass histogram and an alert rule. ops-bot will post top 5 buffer keys and stack hints if outliers detected.

ops-bot: leak-detector alert created: rule 'scoped-leak-high-lifetime' -> posts to #eng-runtime with top samples.

maria: next steps: 1) run 24h canary with LRU recycler + promotion heuristics, 2) enable leak-detector in verbose mode for canary only, 3) add test that simulates high short-request QPS to assert no steady growth.

cheng: i'll add unit test for repin/promotion, and integration test for TTL behavior. also will add tracing tag in alloc log: `alloc: buf_id=%d size=%d scoped=%d req=%s`

lina: i'll schedule the 24h canary on se-staging tonight and watch alloc-traces channel. if stable, we can roll to canary-2 for longer.

nate: thanks all. leaving the patch in draft PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/4427 — please review. i'll post the 24h results tomorrow.

maria: quick note: watch out for increased cost from extra zeroing if TTL too low. we should add a metric for zeroing overhead (bytes_zeroed/sec) to monitor.

cheng: noted. adding metric to runtime telemetry.

lina: thx. ping me if you see regressions in p99.

nate: will do. :thumbsup:
